docs.title: Scan tuning
docs.text: Variable Default Description MAX_RESOURCES_PER_SCAN none (pipeline); scaled from LLM_BUDGET_USD (react) Maximum resources handed to the AI. When unset it is 150 per dollar of LLM budget, between 50 and 1000 (300 at the default $2.00; 500 when the budget is unlimited). The figure comes from a measured run of about $0.0033 per resource, so a default scan uses roughly half the budget. Set it explicitly to override; the report records the value and whether it was explicit or budget. AI_MAX_TOKENS 16000 Output-token limit per model response. Used by all providers; Vertex AI is clamped to 8192 and Azure OpenAI to 16384 (their default models' limits) unless you pass a value in code. If the model is cut off, Argus asks it to submit findings in batches and fails with exit code 3 after 3 cut-offs. AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 600 Request timeout for the Anthropic provider. Timeouts and connection errors are retried with backoff. STRICT_COVERAGE false When true, fail the scan (exit 1) if the resource cap leaves any resources unanalysed, or, before any model call is made, if the plan line says LLM_BUDGET_USD cannot cover every residual candidate. Equivalent to --strict-coverage. ARGUS_BASELINE_RULES true Run the deterministic baseline rules before the model. ARGUS_GATE off Evidence gate before the model: off, shadow or on. For EC2 instances (average CPU at least 20% and at least 1 GiB of network in plus out over the window) and RDS instances (average CPU at least 20% and average connections at least 5), on keeps clearly busy resources away from the model and shadow only counts them (coverage.stages.gate.settled, and settled_but_flagged for the ones the model flagged anyway). Resources with no data, a metrics error or a missing metric are never settled. Keep shadow until settled_but_flagged is 0 on real scans. ARGUS_ENGINE pipeline pipeline: evidence gathered in code, batched model triage (cheaper, covers every cost-bearing resource, repeatable). react: the original tool-calling loop. ARGUS_TRIAGE_BATCH_ITEMS 60 Maximum resources per model call in the pipeline (batches are also limited by size). ARGUS_ACTIVITY_LOOKUP auto Last-activity (CloudTrail) lookups: auto only for resources whose metrics could not decide (at most 150 per scan), all, or off. ARGUS_EXPECT_ACCOUNT unset AWS account ID the credentials must belong to (single-account scans). A mismatch aborts with exit code 4 before any cloud or LLM call. Equivalent to --expect-account. ARGUS_PROGRESS auto Scan progress on stderr for argus scan: auto (a live line in a terminal, plain lines otherwise), plain (always plain lines) or off. Equivalent to --no-progress for off. Deployed runs (Lambda, Cloud Run, Azure Function) never show it. ARGUS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT false When true, skip the pre-scan environment checks (identity, Resource Explorer index/view/permissions). Logged at WARNING and recorded in the report. Equivalent to --skip-preflight. METRICS_LOOKBACK_DAYS 90 CloudWatch / Cloud Monitoring / Azure Monitor lookback window. Applied to every metrics query (the model cannot override it) and recorded in the report's scan_window. 90 days covers quarterly usage patterns and aligns with the CloudTrail lookback. Set to 14 for faster local dev runs — not recommended in production as short windows produce false-positive idle findings. COST_LOOKBACK_DAYS 14 Window for per-resource cost, set with --cost-days. The model cannot override it. AWS resource-level cost data holds at most 14 days, so larger values are capped at 14 on AWS and the report's scan_window.cost_lookback_days shows the effective value. ACTIVITY_LOOKBACK_DAYS 90 Window for last-activity lookups, set with --activity-days. AWS CloudTrail can look back at most 90 days, so larger values are capped at 90. ADAPTER_CONCURRENCY 10 Maximum parallel threads for metric and activity fetches during a scan. Increase for large accounts with many resources; decrease if you hit API rate limits. MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS 50 Maximum ReAct loop iterations before the agent is forced to stop. Increase only if the agent is consistently hitting the limit on very large accounts. LLM_BUDGET_USD 2.00 Hard budget for LLM cost per scan in USD. The scan aborts gracefully if this limit is exceeded, returns partial results, and exits with code 2. Set to 0 to disable the budget check. EXCLUDE_TAGS (empty) JSON object of tags; resources carrying any matching tag are dropped before the AI sees them, e.g. {"argus-exempt": "true"} EXCLUDE_RESOURCE_TYPES (empty) Comma-separated resource types to drop before the AI sees them, e.g. AWS::EC2::Snapshot

docs.title: Secret manager integration
docs.text:
Instead of storing sensitive values directly in environment variables, you can point them to a cloud secret manager. Every argus scan (local or deployed) resolves secret references at startup before any other processing. argus chat does not.

Supported variables: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL, WEBHOOK_URL, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT

Cloud Pattern Example AWS Secrets Manager arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:<name> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:123456789012:secret:argus/api-key GCP Secret Manager gcp-secret://<project>/<secret>[/<version>] SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=gcp-secret://my-project/slack-webhook Azure Key Vault akv://<vault-name>/<secret-name> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=akv://my-vault/anthropic-key

The required SDK must be installed for the cloud you reference — boto3 for AWS, google-cloud-secret-manager for GCP, azure-keyvault-secrets + azure-identity for Azure. If the value doesn't match any pattern, it's used as-is (no SDK required).

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
Variable Default Description REMEDIATION_ENABLED false Opt-in. Set true to create Jira tickets automatically after each scan. argus policies apply --confirm is not affected. ARGUS_POLICY_DIR config/policies Directory containing *.yaml policy files, used by both argus policies and scheduled scans. The older name ARGUS_POLICIES_DIR is still accepted; if both are set, ARGUS_POLICY_DIR wins. ARGUS_INTEGRATIONS_CONFIG config/integrations.yaml Path to integrations config (Jira project key, issue type, labels) ARGUS_AUDIT_LOG ./local_reports/audit.jsonl Path for the append-only proposal audit log JIRA_BASE_URL — Jira instance URL, e.g. https://yourorg.atlassian.net JIRA_USER_EMAIL — Email address associated with the Jira API token JIRA_API_TOKEN — Jira API token (generate at id.atlassian.com)

Note

config/integrations.yaml is gitignored — never commit Jira credentials. JIRA_API_TOKEN is not one of the variables resolved from secret-manager references above; inject it with your platform's own secret mechanism (e.g. Lambda environment encryption, Cloud Run --set-secrets, or an Azure Key Vault app-setting reference).

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
argus scan (and the legacy argus --run-now) exits with one of these codes. Orchestrators such as cron wrappers, CI jobs and Cloud Run Jobs can tell the failure modes apart without parsing output.

Code Meaning What to do 0 Scan finished and findings were submitted (possibly an explicit empty list). Nothing. 1 Configuration or runtime error, or --strict-coverage / STRICT_COVERAGE=true and the resource cap left resources unanalysed, or the budget cannot cover every residual candidate (stopped before any model spend). Read the message on stderr. For coverage, raise MAX_RESOURCES_PER_SCAN. 2 The LLM budget (--llm-budget, default $2.00) was exceeded and the scan aborted. Raise the budget or lower MAX_RESOURCES_PER_SCAN. 3 The model stopped without calling submit_findings, even after one reminder. The scan is treated as failed, not as "no findings". Re-run. If it repeats, check the model/provider and the logs. 4 Preflight failed: the environment would give silently partial or empty results (for example no Resource Explorer aggregator index). No LLM budget was spent. Follow the fix printed for each failed check, see Troubleshooting.

In AWS Lambda, Cloud Run and Azure Functions there is no process exit code for every case: failures surface as an invocation error with the same message.

docs.title: IAM Permissions
docs.text: Argus requires read-only permissions. No write permissions are ever requested.

docs.title: AWS
docs.text: The policies below are taken from the CloudFormation templates in deploy/aws/. Deploying the templates creates them for you.

docs.title: Lambda execution role (single account)
docs.text:
deploy/aws/single-account/template.yaml creates ArgusLambdaRole-<region> with:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "resource-explorer-2:Search",
        "resource-explorer-2:GetView",
        "resource-explorer-2:ListIndexes",
        "resource-explorer-2:ListSupportedResourceTypes",
        "resource-explorer-2:GetIndex",
        "resource-explorer-2:GetDefaultView",
        "resource-explorer-2:ListViews",
        "cloudwatch:GetMetricData",
        "cloudwatch:ListMetrics",
        "ce:GetCostAndUsage",
        "ce:GetCostAndUsageWithResources",
        "cloudtrail:LookupEvents",
        "tag:GetResources",
        "ec2:DescribeInstances",
        "ec2:DescribeVolumes",
        "ec2:DescribeSnapshots",
        "ec2:DescribeImages",
        "logs:DescribeLogGroups",
        "logs:DescribeLogStreams",
        "rds:DescribeDBSnapshots",
        "rds:DescribeDBClusterSnapshots",
        "ec2:DescribeAddresses",
        "rds:DescribeDBInstances",
        "rds:DescribeDBClusters",
        "elasticache:DescribeCacheClusters",
        "elasticache:DescribeReplicationGroups",
        "redshift:DescribeClusters",
        "es:DescribeDomain",
        "lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration",
        "dms:DescribeReplicationInstances",
        "sts:GetCallerIdentity"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "bedrock:InvokeModel",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock:<BedrockRegion>::foundation-model/<BedrockModelId>"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:GetObject"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::argus-reports-<account>-<region>/*"
    }
  ]
}

Why the extra Resource Explorer permissions?

Before every scan Argus runs a preflight that checks the aggregator index (ListIndexes, GetIndex), the default view and its tags property (GetDefaultView, GetView), and that Search works. Without them the scan stops with exit code 4 and a message naming what is missing. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Dedicated read-only scan role
docs.text:
Two ways to give a person or CI job a scan role that is not an administrator:

Option Policy When to use Minimal (default) Only the actions listed above Least privilege; what Argus actually calls ReadOnlyAccess + additions AWS managed ReadOnlyAccess plus the Resource Explorer and Cost Explorer actions Easier to audit against a standard policy. ReadOnlyAccess alone is not enough: it does not include the Resource Explorer actions Argus needs

deploy/aws/read-only-scan-role.yaml creates either variant (UseAwsReadOnlyAccess=true|false). Then scan with a guard against a wrong profile:

argus scan --cloud aws --expect-account 123456789012

--expect-account (or ARGUS_EXPECT_ACCOUNT) aborts with exit code 4 before any cloud or LLM call when the credentials belong to a different account. It applies to single-account scans.

Do not scan with an administrator role. A copy-paste Terraform role with exactly the permissions above is in deploy/aws/terraform/read-only-scan-role.tf; the CloudFormation templates in deploy/aws/ create the same set. Argus prints the identity it runs as at the start of every scan and warns when the name looks like Administrator* or *FullAccess.

Why the describe permissions?

Argus uses these read-only Describe* calls to fetch the current instance size (e.g. db.r5.4xlarge, cache.r6g.xlarge) during metric collection. Without this, the AI can only say "consider downsizing." With it, the AI says "RIGHT-SIZE: db.r5.4xlarge → db.r5.2xlarge, saving ~$280/month." All calls are read-only and never modify any resource.

Why ec2:DescribeSnapshots and ec2:DescribeImages?

Before a snapshot is suggested for deletion, Argus checks whether an AMI still uses it. Without these two actions, snapshot details cannot be read and snapshot findings are withheld from the waste total (listed under coverage.withheld as state_unavailable) rather than reported. elasticache:DescribeReplicationGroups and elasticache:DescribeCacheClusters play the same role for cache nodes.

Why logs:DescribeLogStreams and rds:DescribeDBSnapshots?

CloudTrail does not record log ingestion, so Argus reads a log group's newest stream (logs:DescribeLogStreams) to know when it last received events. If that call is denied, log-group findings are withheld (activity_unverified), never reported as idle. rds:DescribeDBSnapshots and rds:DescribeDBClusterSnapshots tell automated snapshots from manual ones; without them RDS snapshot findings are withheld (state_unavailable).

cloudwatch:ListMetrics powers the dynamic metric discovery used for resource types that aren't in the registry.

docs.title: Hub role (multi-account)
docs.text: deploy/aws/multi-account/hub/template.yaml creates ArgusHubRole-<region>. It scans nothing itself; it only needs sts:AssumeRole on the spoke roles, sts:GetCallerIdentity, bedrock:InvokeModel, and s3:PutObject / s3:GetObject on the report bucket.

docs.title: Spoke role (multi-account)
docs.text:
deploy/aws/multi-account/spoke-role.yaml creates ArgusSpokeRole in each target account with the same read-only scan permissions as the single-account role (without Bedrock, S3, or STS):

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "resource-explorer-2:Search",
        "resource-explorer-2:GetView",
        "resource-explorer-2:ListIndexes",
        "cloudwatch:GetMetricData",
        "cloudwatch:ListMetrics",
        "ce:GetCostAndUsage",
        "ce:GetCostAndUsageWithResources",
        "cloudtrail:LookupEvents",
        "ec2:DescribeInstances",
        "rds:DescribeDBInstances",
        "rds:DescribeDBClusters",
        "elasticache:DescribeCacheClusters",
        "elasticache:DescribeReplicationGroups",
        "redshift:DescribeClusters",
        "es:DescribeDomain",
        "lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration",
        "dms:DescribeReplicationInstances"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Trust policy — allows only the hub role (the HubRoleArn output of the hub stack) to assume it:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::<HUB_ACCOUNT_ID>:role/ArgusHubRole-<region>"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}

Cost Explorer requires activation

ce:GetCostAndUsageWithResources requires:

  1. Cost Explorer activated for your account
  2. Resource-level data enabled: Cost Management → Preferences → Resource-level data

If not set up, Argus logs a warning and continues with $0.00 cost values.

docs.title: GCP
docs.text:
The Cloud Run service account (argus-sa@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com) needs:

Role Purpose roles/cloudasset.viewer List all resources via Asset Inventory roles/monitoring.viewer Read Cloud Monitoring metrics roles/logging.viewer Read Cloud Audit Logs roles/bigquery.dataViewer Query BigQuery billing export roles/bigquery.jobUser Run BigQuery jobs roles/aiplatform.user Call Vertex AI Gemini (only if AI_PROVIDER=vertexai) roles/storage.objectCreator + roles/storage.objectViewer (bucket) Upload reports (only if REPORT_GCS_BUCKET is set) roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (on the SA itself) Sign the report URL (only if REPORT_GCS_BUCKET is set)

docs.title: Azure
docs.text:
The Function App managed identity needs:

Role Scope Purpose Granted by Bicep? Reader Each subscription to scan Resource Graph, Monitor metrics, Activity Log No — grant manually Cost Management Reader Each subscription to scan Read cost data Resource group only — grant per subscription manually Monitoring Reader Resource group Read Azure Monitor metrics (also covered by Reader) Yes Log Analytics Reader Log Analytics workspace Activity Log KQL queries (only if AZURE_LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_ID is set) No Storage Blob Data Contributor + Storage Blob Delegator Report storage account Upload reports and sign the SAS link (only if REPORT_STORAGE_ACCOUNT is set) Yes, when reportStorageAccount is passed

Granting subscription-level roles

The Bicep template only grants roles at the resource group level. For each subscription you want to scan, run:

for ROLE in "Reader" "Cost Management Reader"; do
  az role assignment create \
    --assignee <principalId> \
    --role "$ROLE" \
    --scope /subscriptions/<subscription-id>
done

docs.title: Report JSON Schema
docs.text:
Version: 1.2.0

Every Argus scan produces a JSON report with the following top-level fields.

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text: Field Type Description schema_version string Schema version identifier. Currently "1.2.0". scan_id string UUID v4 unique to this scan. generated_at string ISO 8601 timestamp (UTC) when the report was generated. cloud string Cloud provider: "aws", "gcp", or "azure". accounts_scanned string[] List of account/project/subscription IDs scanned. total_estimated_waste_usd number Sum of all findings' estimated_monthly_cost, rounded to 2 decimal places. findings_count integer Number of findings in this report. findings Finding[] Array of finding objects, sorted by estimated_monthly_cost descending. executive_summary string AI-generated 3–5 sentence summary for non-technical stakeholders. agent_input_tokens integer Total input tokens consumed by the AI agent during this scan. agent_output_tokens integer Total output tokens consumed by the AI agent during this scan. estimated_agent_cost_usd number Estimated AI cost for this scan in USD. scan_diff ScanDiff Cross-scan comparison data. On the first scan (no previous report found), previous_scan_id is null and every finding counts as new. scan_errors object[] Accounts/projects/subscriptions that failed to scan: {account_id, account_name, error}. Empty when all succeeded. skipped_resource_types string[] Resource types that were skipped during the scan (for example, GCP asset types whose API isn't enabled). registry_warnings string[] Invalid resource-registry entries skipped at load time. Normally empty. coverage Coverage \| null What the scan actually analysed. See Coverage object. null when the entrypoint could not provide it. Added in 1.1.0. scan_window object \| null Settings actually used: metrics_lookback_days, cost_lookback_days (the effective cost window, at most 14 on AWS), activity_lookback_days, cost_basis, max_resources and max_resources_source (explicit or budget), tags_source (resource_explorer, tagging_api or unavailable), and the LLM economics llm_budget_usd, llm_estimate_usd (computed before the first call), llm_spent_usd, llm_plan (candidates, covered, full_estimate_usd, covered_estimate_usd, order and the printed line: what the budget buys before any call) and llm_calibration (estimated against actual tokens per model call, counts only). With several accounts llm_plan and llm_calibration are per account and left out of the merged block. Added in 1.1.0. preflight object \| null Results of the pre-scan environment checks. Added in 1.1.0. waste_by_confidence object total_estimated_waste_usd split into high, medium, low and unrated (findings with no confidence). Added in 1.1.0. total_is_estimate boolean true unless every finding's cost_basis is billed; headlines then say the total is not billed. Added in 1.1.0. cost_summary object Where the dollars come from. waste_by_basis (USD per billed, list_price, model_estimate, unknown; adds up to total_estimated_waste_usd), findings_by_basis (counts), unpriced_findings (findings with no dollar figure; shown as unpriced, never as a billed zero), verified_waste_usd (the billed part), verified_share (billed share of the total, null when the total is 0) and headline_is_verified (true when verified_share is at least 0.5, a provisional threshold, or there is nothing to total). Headlines call the total "billed waste", "estimated waste" or "unverified waste estimate" accordingly. Added in 1.2.0. opportunities Opportunity[] Findings grouped into decisions. Every finding is in exactly one. See Opportunity object and Opportunities. Added in 1.2.0. opportunity_summary object findings, opportunities, reduction_ratio (null with no findings), lanes (easy and doubt counts), largest_members, other_bucket_members, min_group_size (the size actually used) and max_opportunities. Added in 1.2.0. findings_needing_review integer Findings whose review_required is true. waste_needs_review_usd number Summed monthly USD of those findings; part of total_estimated_waste_usd, shown separately so it is not read as a safe saving.

docs.title: Coverage object
docs.text: Field Type Description discovered integer Billable resources found after exclusion filters. analysed integer Resources handed to the AI. dropped integer discovered - analysed. truncated boolean true when dropped > 0 (the MAX_RESOURCES_PER_SCAN cap bit). selection string "cost_desc" (cost data available), "stratified_by_type" (round-robin across types) or "mixed" (multi-account). cost_data_available boolean Whether any per-resource cost was returned. regions_covered string[] Regions in the discovered inventory. types object Per resource type: {discovered, analysed}. stop_reason string \| null Why not everything was analysed: "budget", "cap" or "llm_failure"; null when complete. skipped_by_reason object Resources not analysed, by reason (budget, cap, llm_failure). free_config_skipped integer Free configuration objects (subnets, IAM roles, ...) skipped on purpose; not part of discovered. metrics_lost_to_throttling integer Resources whose metrics could not be fetched because the cloud API kept throttling after retries. withheld array Model findings left out of the waste total because the evidence could not support them. Each item has resource_id, resource_type, kind (no_metrics, failover_replica, state_unavailable, ami_backed, protected_by_tag, recent_log_activity, activity_unverified, automated_snapshot) and reason. Additive. stages object \| null The same scan per stage. rules: evaluated, findings, undecided. gate: mode (off, shadow, on), settled, and in shadow mode settled_but_flagged (settled resources the model flagged anyway; the gate is only safe to enable when this stays 0). model: candidates (what the model still owed after rules), analysed, skipped, stop_reason and order (billed_cost when any billed cost exists; else list_price when a list-price stand-in was available, used for ordering only and never shown as a cost; else type_risk). A partial model pass is read against model.candidates, not against discovered. discovery_complete boolean \| null false when a discovery query hit the provider's result limit (AWS Resource Explorer returns at most 1,000 per query; Argus then searches region by region and sets this only if a single region still overflows). null when the adapter does not report it. Added in 1.1.0.

docs.title: Finding object
docs.text: Field Type Description resource_id string Cloud-native resource identifier (ARN, self-link, or resource ID). resource_type string Registry type ID (e.g. "AWS::EC2::Instance", "sqladmin.googleapis.com/Instance", "microsoft.compute/virtualmachines"). See Resource Types. cloud string Cloud provider. region string Region or location where the resource exists. name string \| null Human-readable name tag, if available. estimated_monthly_cost number Estimated monthly cost in USD. waste_reason string AI-written explanation of why the resource is considered idle. recommendation string AI-written recommended action (delete, resize, tag, etc.). priority string "high", "medium", or "low" — assigned by the AI. metrics_summary object Key metric signals the AI used to make its decision. tags object Resource tags as key-value pairs. confidence string \| null "low", "medium" or "high". Forced to low when the metrics behind the finding were unavailable; capped at medium for windows under 90 days. Added in 1.1.0. cost_basis string \| null Where the dollar figure comes from: "billed" (Cost Explorer), "list_price" (Argus price catalog, us-east-1 list prices), "model_estimate" (the AI's guess) or "unknown" (no figure). Reports written before 1.1.0 may carry "estimated" or no value; readers treat those as model_estimate when there is a dollar figure and as unknown when there is not. Added in 1.1.0. review_required boolean true when a human must check this finding before any ticket, deletion or resize: the name looks like production (prod, prd, production, live, critical, "do not touch") or the estimate is at least $1,000/month with no billed cost behind it. Added in 1.1.0. review_reasons string[] Why: prod_like_name, high_unbilled_estimate. Empty when review_required is false. detected_by string \| null "model" or "rule:<id>" for a baseline rule. Added in 1.1.0. last_activity string \| null ISO 8601 timestamp of the last detected activity, or null. scan_time string ISO 8601 timestamp of when the resource was scanned. account_id string \| null Account / project / subscription the resource belongs to. Added in 1.0.1; null if it couldn't be attributed. account_name string \| null Display name for account_id (from accounts.yaml / ACCOUNTS_CONFIG, else the ID). Added in 1.0.1. status string "new" or "recurring", set by cross-scan comparison. Resolved resources aren't in findings; they're listed in scan_diff.resolved_resource_ids.

docs.title: ScanDiff object
docs.text: Field Type Description previous_scan_id string \| null Scan ID of the previous report used for comparison. new_findings integer Count of findings not present in the previous scan. recurring_findings integer Count of findings present in both scans. resolved_findings integer Count of findings from the previous scan no longer present. resolved_resource_ids string[] Resource IDs that were in the previous scan but not this one.

docs.title: Versioning policy
docs.text:
The schema_version field uses semantic versioning:

  • Patch (1.0.x): new optional fields added. Existing consumers are unaffected.
  • Minor (1.x.0): new optional top-level blocks, changed field semantics, or optional fields becoming required.
  • Major (x.0.0): fields removed or renamed. Consumers must update.

Consumers should check schema_version before parsing and handle unknown versions gracefully.

Version Change 1.1.0 (v0.7.0) New optional top-level coverage, scan_window and preflight blocks. Nothing removed or renamed. 1.0.1 (v0.6.0) Findings gained optional account_id and account_name. 1.0 Initial schema.

docs.title: Opportunity object
docs.text: Field Type Description id string opp- plus 12 hex characters, a hash of key. Stable across scans. key object action, family (a resource type, snapshot or other) and tier (flagged, unsure or sure). title string Plain template, for example Remove 3 EBS Volumes. action string remove, stop, rightsize, retention or review. lane string easy or doubt. resource_types string[] Types of the members. accounts, regions string[] Where the members are. owners object[] Up to five {tag, value, count} from the team, owner, project, application, service tags. unowned_count integer Members with none of those tags. member_count, members integer, string[] All member resource ids, highest cost first. savings object low_usd, high_usd, by_basis and unpriced; see Opportunities. priority, confidence string Highest member priority; lowest member confidence. review_required_count integer Members flagged for human review. evidence string[] Plain sentences from the members' own data: how many came from rules and how many from model review, how many have metrics and activity checks, dollars by cost basis, lowest confidence. risk string One paragraph: what can go wrong with the action, plus any review flags, low confidence and unpriced members. check_first string[] Steps to take before acting, by action and resource family. Templates, not model output. risk_reasons string[] Union of the members' review_reasons. related string[] Ids of opportunities whose findings name these resources.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: Argus is designed to be safe to deploy in production environments. This page documents the security boundaries and data handling.

docs.title: Read-only access
docs.text:
Argus uses read-only IAM roles on every cloud. It cannot modify, delete, or create any resources in your account. The specific permissions are documented on the IAM Permissions page.

Cloud Auth method Scope AWS IAM execution role (Lambda) or assumed role (multi-account) Read-only: Resource Explorer, CloudWatch, Cost Explorer, CloudTrail, Describe APIs (plus s3:PutObject on its own report bucket) GCP Service account with viewer roles Read-only: Asset Inventory, Monitoring, Logging, BigQuery Azure System-assigned managed identity Read-only: Resource Graph, Monitor, Cost Management, Activity Log

docs.title: Data collected
docs.text:
During a scan, Argus reads:

  • Resource metadata — IDs, types, regions, tags, creation dates
  • Usage metrics — CPU, network, disk I/O, connections (aggregated, not per-request)
  • Cost data — estimated monthly cost per resource in USD
  • Activity timestamps — when each resource was last accessed or modified

Argus does not read:

  • File contents, database records, or application data
  • Network traffic or request logs
  • Secrets, keys, or credentials stored in your resources
  • PII or customer data

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Cloud APIs → Argus agent (in-memory) ⇄ AI provider → Report
                                                        ↓
                                              Storage (S3/GCS/Blob) + local copy
                                                        ↓
                                     Jira tickets (only if REMEDIATION_ENABLED=true)
                                                        ↓
                                        Slack / Teams / webhook digest
  1. Resource data is fetched from cloud APIs and held in memory during the scan
  2. A compact resource list (IDs, names, types, regions, costs) is sent to the AI provider, which then requests metrics and last-activity data for the candidates it chooses to investigate. This is a multi-turn conversation (up to MAX_AGENT_ITERATIONS calls), plus one call for the executive summary
  3. The AI returns findings with waste reasons and recommendations
  4. A JSON + HTML report is saved to LOCAL_REPORT_DIR and, if configured, to cloud storage
  5. If REMEDIATION_ENABLED=true and policies match, Jira tickets are created with the finding details
  6. A compact digest is posted with a link to the full report
  7. In-memory data is discarded when the process exits

docs.title: Data retention
docs.text: Location Retention Encryption Cloud storage (S3/GCS/Blob) 90 days on S3 (lifecycle rule in the SAM templates); no lifecycle rule is set on GCS or Blob by default — add one if you need it Encrypted at rest (cloud-native SSE) Local report copies (LOCAL_REPORT_DIR) Until deleted; ephemeral on Lambda / Cloud Run / Functions Filesystem Jira tickets and audit.jsonl (remediation) Controlled by your Jira instance / until deleted Jira's encryption / filesystem Pre-signed/SAS URLs 7 days (configurable via REPORT_URL_EXPIRY) HTTPS in transit Slack messages Controlled by your Slack workspace retention policy Slack's encryption Lambda/Cloud Run/Function memory Ephemeral — discarded after each invocation N/A

docs.title: AI provider data handling
docs.text:
The AI calls send compact resource data (IDs, names, types, regions, tags, metrics, costs, last-activity timestamps) — not raw cloud API responses. No credentials, secrets, or application data are included.

Provider Data path Retention AWS Bedrock Stays in your AWS account. Model invocation logs are off by default. No training on your data (AWS policy) Anthropic API Sent to Anthropic's API endpoint. Not used for training. See Anthropic's privacy policy Vertex AI / Azure OpenAI Stays in your cloud account Governed by your cloud provider agreement

docs.title: Credential handling
docs.text:
• No hardcoded credentials — all auth is via environment variables or cloud-native IAM roles
  • Multi-account STS sessions — temporary credentials, 1-hour expiry, never stored to disk
  • Webhook URLs — marked NoEcho (AWS) / @secure() (Azure) in deploy templates
  • API keys — stored in environment variables, never logged

docs.title: Network access
docs.text:
Argus makes outbound HTTPS calls to:

  1. Your cloud provider's APIs (same account/project/subscription)
  2. The configured AI provider endpoint
  3. The notification endpoints you configure (Slack / Teams / generic webhook)
  4. Cloud storage for report upload
  5. Your Jira instance (only when remediation creates tickets)

No inbound network access is required. The Lambda/Cloud Run/Function does not expose any HTTP endpoints.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common issues and their solutions.

docs.title: Resource Explorer: "No aggregator index found" or 401 Unauthorized on Search
docs.text:
Argus needs an aggregator index and a default view in RESOURCE_EXPLORER_REGION (default us-east-1). Search fails with 401 Unauthorized if the region has no default view. Create both:

aws resource-explorer-2 create-index --region us-east-1
INDEX_ARN=$(aws resource-explorer-2 get-index --region us-east-1 --query Arn --output text)
aws resource-explorer-2 update-index-type --arn "$INDEX_ARN" --type AGGREGATOR --region us-east-1

# Search uses the region's default view; include tags so Argus sees them
VIEW_ARN=$(aws resource-explorer-2 create-view --view-name argus-all \
  --included-properties Name=tags --region us-east-1 --query View.ViewArn --output text)
aws resource-explorer-2 associate-default-view --view-arn "$VIEW_ARN" --region us-east-1

The aggregator index can take a while to replicate resources from all regions after it's created. If resources show no tags, the default view is missing the tags property.

docs.title: Cost Explorer: "OptInRequired" or all costs show $0
docs.text:
Cost Explorer must be activated in the AWS console before the API works:

  1. Go to AWS Cost Management → Cost Explorer
  2. Click Launch Cost Explorer (one-time activation, takes up to 24 hours)

docs.title: Bedrock: "AccessDeniedException" for model invocation
docs.text:
You need to enable model access in the Bedrock console:

  1. Go to Amazon Bedrock → Model catalog (or search "Bedrock" in the AWS console and open Model access from the left nav)
  2. Find Claude Sonnet (Anthropic) and click Request access / Enable
  3. Access is usually granted instantly for Sonnet

Make sure BEDROCK_REGION matches the region where you enabled model access.

docs.title: Bedrock: "INVALID_PAYMENT_INSTRUMENT"
docs.text:
This is a billing issue, not an IAM issue. AWS requires a valid payment method on the account before Bedrock can be used.

  1. Go to AWS Console → Account Settings → Payment methods
  2. Add or verify a payment method
  3. Wait ~1 minute for it to propagate, then retry the scan

docs.title: Azure OpenAI: 400 BadRequest for o4-mini / o1 / o3 deployments
docs.text:
Reasoning models require a newer API version than the default (2024-10-21):

AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-12-01-preview

Argus automatically retries without temperature when a reasoning model rejects it — no extra config needed for that.

Note

Check Azure OpenAI API releases for the latest stable version that supports your model.

docs.title: Pre-signed URL returns 403
docs.text: The Lambda role needs both s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on the report bucket. The SAM templates include both — if you customized IAM, verify the S3Reports policy statement.

docs.title: "Cloud Asset API has not been enabled"
docs.text:
The deploy script enables these APIs automatically (but not Vertex AI). If running manually:

gcloud services enable \
  cloudasset.googleapis.com \
  monitoring.googleapis.com \
  logging.googleapis.com \
  bigquery.googleapis.com \
  --project=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT

For the default AI_PROVIDER=vertexai, also enable aiplatform.googleapis.com.

docs.title: Billing data shows $0 for all resources
docs.text:
BigQuery billing export must be enabled:

  1. Go to GCP Console → Billing → Billing export → BigQuery export
  2. Note the full table name (format: project.dataset.gcp_billing_export_v1_XXXXXX)
  3. Set BILLING_BQ_TABLE to the table name

docs.title: Signed URL error: "iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob permission"
docs.text:
v4 signed URLs require the service account to have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on itself. The deploy script handles this, but if you configured IAM manually:

gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding \
  argus-sa@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="serviceAccount:argus-sa@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

docs.title: "AuthorizationFailed" on subscription scan
docs.text:
The managed identity needs Reader (and Cost Management Reader for cost data) at the subscription level. The Bicep template only assigns roles at the resource group level — you must grant subscription-level roles manually:

az role assignment create \
  --assignee $PRINCIPAL_ID \
  --role "Reader" \
  --scope /subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID

docs.title: SAS URL returns 403
docs.text:
The managed identity needs two roles on the report storage account:

  • Storage Blob Data Contributor — read/write blobs
  • Storage Blob Delegator — required for get_user_delegation_key()

The Bicep template assigns both when reportStorageAccount is set.

docs.title: Azure Functions Core Tools: "command not found"
docs.text:
Install the Azure Functions Core Tools v4:

# macOS
brew tap azure/functions
brew install azure-functions-core-tools@4

# npm (any OS)
npm install -g azure-functions-core-tools@4

docs.title: Webhook returns HTTP 403 or "invalid_token"
docs.text:
• Verify the webhook URL is correct and hasn't been revoked
  • Check that the Slack app hasn't been uninstalled from the workspace
  • Create a new webhook at api.slack.com/apps

docs.title: Webhook returns HTTP 429
docs.text: Slack rate-limits incoming webhooks to ~1 message per second. Argus sends one message per scan, so this shouldn't happen unless you're running multiple scans simultaneously.

docs.title: "SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is not set"
docs.text:
Every argus scan (local or deployed) checks for SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL at startup, even if you only send to Teams or a generic webhook via NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER. For local dev, add it to your .env file. For cloud deploys, it's set via the CloudFormation/Bicep/deploy.sh parameters.

To skip delivery during development, set DRY_RUN=true.

docs.title: Scan finds zero resources
docs.text:
• AWS: Verify Resource Explorer has an aggregator index and a default view in RESOURCE_EXPLORER_REGION, and has finished indexing
  • All clouds: Check EXCLUDE_TAGS / EXCLUDE_RESOURCE_TYPES / IGNORE_REGIONS aren't filtering everything out
  • GCP: Verify GCP_PROJECT_ID is set and the service account has roles/cloudasset.viewer
  • Azure: Verify AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_IDS lists valid subscription IDs and Reader is granted

docs.title: Preflight checks
docs.text: Before every AWS scan Argus checks the environment and stops (exit code 4) when a result would be silently partial. Each failure prints the fix; this page explains the codes. --skip-preflight (or ARGUS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=true) bypasses the checks, which is recorded in the report.

docs.title: P1_IDENTITY
docs.text: Information, or a warning when the caller's name looks like Administrator* or *FullAccess (a name-based check only; Argus makes no IAM calls to inspect policies). Scan with a dedicated read-only role: see IAM Permissions.

docs.title: P2_RE_REACHABLE
docs.text: Argus cannot list Resource Explorer indexes. Grant resource-explorer-2:ListIndexes (the full set is in IAM Permissions).

docs.title: P3_AGGREGATOR_INDEX
docs.text: Only local indexes exist (a search then covers one region and silently misses the rest), none exist, or the aggregator is in another region. Create an aggregator index in RESOURCE_EXPLORER_REGION, or set that variable to the region that has one. Commands are in the first section of this page.

docs.title: P4_INDEX_STATE
docs.text: Warning: the index is CREATING or UPDATING, so results may be partial. Wait until it is ACTIVE, then re-run.

docs.title: P5_DEFAULT_VIEW
docs.text: Warning: there is no default view in the aggregator region (or it cannot be read). Search still works, but results carry no tags, so policy excludes such as environment: prod and argus-exempt cannot work. Create a view that includes the tags property and associate it as the default (first section of this page).

docs.title: P6_VIEW_TAGS
docs.text: Warning: the default view does not include the tags property. Every resource looks untagged, so policy excludes such as environment: prod and argus-exempt cannot work. Add Name=tags to the view's included properties.

docs.title: P8_COST_DATA
docs.text: Warning: per-resource cost data is unavailable (resource-level data is not enabled, Cost Explorer is not activated, or the role lacks ce:GetCostAndUsageWithResources). Scans still run, but findings carry no billed cost (cost_basis: estimated). Enable resource-level data in the PAYER account: Cost Management > Cost Explorer settings > Resource-level data. Resource-level data covers only the last 14 days, so Argus requests at most 14 days of it.

docs.title: P9_STATE_ACCESS
docs.text: Warning: the scan role cannot call ec2:DescribeVolumes and/or ec2:DescribeAddresses. Scans still run, but the rules that find unattached EBS volumes, unassociated Elastic IPs and stopped instances are off, because those wastes leave no metric trace. Add the named actions to the role (see IAM Permissions).

docs.title: Resource Explorer's 1,000-result limit
docs.text: Resource Explorer Search returns at most 1,000 results in total. On larger accounts Argus logs resource_explorer_search_limit and the report's coverage.discovered can understate the real inventory. Argus then searches region by region, and splits a region that is still full by service and resource type (this needs resource-explorer-2:ListSupportedResourceTypes; without it coverage.discovery_complete is reported as false because services it has not seen cannot be ruled out). If a single resource type in one region still exceeds 1,000 resources, discovery_complete is false.

docs.title: P7_SEARCH_PERMISSION
docs.text: Search was denied or failed. The scan role needs resource-explorer-2:Search, GetView, GetDefaultView, ListViews, ListIndexes and GetIndex.

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Argus is strictly read-only — it never modifies a resource. The remediation system turns AI findings into prioritised Jira tickets that a human reviews and executes.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
argus scan   →   scan_report.json
                       │
                       ▼
argus policies plan    →   proposal table (dry run — no tickets created)
                       │
                       ▼  (add --confirm)
argus policies apply   →   Jira tickets + audit log entry per proposal
                       │
                       ▼  (ongoing)
argus policies stats   →   acceptance rate per policy from audit log

docs.title: Key properties
docs.text: Property Detail Human gate Runbooks are printed in Jira tickets — Argus never executes them Idempotent Re-running apply on the same findings updates existing tickets, not new ones Audit trail Every create/update event appended to local_reports/audit.jsonl — never overwritten Rightsizing resize and reduce_nodes proposals include a specific target tier or node count Policy count 13 bundled policies across AWS, GCP, and Azure

docs.title: Required environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose Default REMEDIATION_ENABLED Set true to create tickets automatically after each scan. Not needed for argus policies apply --confirm false ARGUS_POLICY_DIR Directory containing your *.yaml policy files ./config/policies JIRA_BASE_URL Your Jira instance URL (e.g. https://org.atlassian.net) — JIRA_USER_EMAIL Bot account email for ticket creation — JIRA_API_TOKEN Atlassian API token (not your password) — ARGUS_INTEGRATIONS_CONFIG Path to integrations.yaml (project key, labels, priority map) ./config/integrations.yaml ARGUS_AUDIT_LOG Path for the JSONL audit log ./local_reports/audit.jsonl

See .env.example for the full list with comments.

docs.text:

  • Jira Integration — setup, ticket lifecycle, ADF description, dedup

docs.title: CLI Reference — argus policies
docs.text: All remediation commands are under the argus policies subcommand.

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Check all policies in a directory for errors and warnings before running a plan.

argus policies validate --dir config/policies

Options

Flag Default Description --dir ARGUS_POLICY_DIR or ./config/policies Directory containing *.yaml policy files

Exit codes

Code Meaning 0 All policies valid (warnings printed but not fatal) 1 One or more errors (files that fail to load, duplicate IDs, invalid actions, weight conflicts, etc.)

Example output

  ✓ aws-ebs-delete-unattached.yaml  weight: 15    resource: AWS::EC2::Volume
  ✓ aws-ec2-stop-idle.yaml          weight: 10    resource: AWS::EC2::Instance
  ...
  ✓ gcp-sql-stop-idle.yaml          weight: 20    resource: sqladmin.googleapis.com/Instance

13 policies loaded — 0 error(s), 0 warning(s).

A file that fails to load is reported with the reason, e.g. ✗ bad.yaml: invalid action 'fly'. Must be one of: [...]. Warnings (such as a lower-weight policy that is fully shadowed by a higher-weight one) are printed but don't fail validation.

docs.title: plan
docs.text:
Evaluate policies against a scan report and print the proposal table. Dry run — no tickets created.

argus policies plan --report local_reports/aws/2026/09/27/<scan-id>.json
argus policies plan --live --cloud aws      # run a fresh scan instead (incurs API/AI cost)

Options

Flag Default Description --report — Path to an existing scan report JSON (fast, no cloud calls) --live off Run a live scan instead of reading --report --cloud — aws | gcp | azure — required with --live --dir ARGUS_POLICY_DIR or ./config/policies Policy directory

One of --report or --live is required.

Example output

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             POLICY PLAN — scan.json — 2026-09-27                    │
│              3 finding(s) · 13 policies · 2 match(es)               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  POLICY                 RESOURCE                COST/MO  ACTION
  ─────────────────────  ─────────────────────  ────────  ──────────────
  ● aws-ec2-stop-idle-14d  i-0abc123def                $28  stop
  ● aws-ebs-delete-unatta  vol-orphan-0def8             $8  snapshot_delete

  – aws-elasticache-delete-idle-30d  (no findings matched)
  ...

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  2 match(es)  ·  Potential savings: $36/mo

  Jira ticket preview (2 ticket(s) would be created):
  · [Argus] Stop i-0abc123def ($28/mo · high priority)
  · [Argus] Snapshot & delete vol-orphan-0def8 ($8/mo · medium priority)

  Next step: Run with --confirm to create Jira tickets.

For resize and reduce_nodes matches, a rightsizing hint such as ↳ Recommend db.t3.small (observed CPU ~8.0%) is shown under the row.

Priority dots: 🔴 high · 🟡 medium · ⚪ low

docs.title: apply
docs.text:
Same as plan but creates Jira tickets when --confirm is passed.

# Dry run (same as plan)
argus policies apply --report local_reports/scan.json

# Create tickets
argus policies apply --report local_reports/scan.json --confirm

Options

Flag Default Description --report — Path to an existing scan report JSON --live / --cloud off Run a live scan instead (same as plan) --dir ARGUS_POLICY_DIR or ./config/policies Policy directory --confirm false Create/update Jira tickets (requires Jira env vars)

apply --confirm works regardless of REMEDIATION_ENABLED; that setting only controls automatic tickets after scheduled scans.

Required env vars (when --confirm is set)

JIRA_BASE_URL=https://yourorg.atlassian.net
JIRA_USER_EMAIL=you@yourorg.com
JIRA_API_TOKEN=your-token
ARGUS_INTEGRATIONS_CONFIG=config/integrations.yaml

Example output (with --confirm)

  ✓ vol-orphan-0def8  →  https://yourorg.atlassian.net/browse/COST-38

A resource that already has an open ticket shows that ticket's URL; no duplicate is created.

docs.title: Jira Integration
docs.text: Argus creates Jira tickets for approved proposals. Each ticket contains the AI reasoning, key metrics, a copy-paste runbook, and a rightsizing recommendation (for resize/reduce_nodes actions).

docs.title: 1 — Policy directory
docs.text:
Tell Argus where your policy files live:

export ARGUS_POLICY_DIR=./config/policies   # default — already correct if you use the repo layout

Not set? Argus silently skips remediation and only posts the scan digest to Slack. Copy starter templates from config/policies.example/ to get going quickly.

docs.title: 2 — Jira API token
docs.text:
Generate an API token at id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens and set these env vars:

export JIRA_BASE_URL=https://yourorg.atlassian.net
export JIRA_USER_EMAIL=you@yourorg.com
export JIRA_API_TOKEN=your-token-here

docs.title: 3 — Turn on automatic tickets (optional)
docs.text:
argus policies apply --confirm creates tickets on demand with just the steps above. To have every scheduled scan create tickets as well, opt in:

export REMEDIATION_ENABLED=true   # default: false

If Jira credentials are set but this is off, the scan logs remediation_skipped reason=disabled with a hint, and still delivers the Slack digest. With DRY_RUN=true, an enabled scan logs what it would track and makes no Jira calls.

docs.title: 4 — Integrations config
docs.text:
Create config/integrations.yaml (gitignored — never commit this):

Start from config/integrations.yaml.example:

version: "1"

jira:
  project: COST                 # required — Jira project key where tickets are created
  issue_type: Task              # optional (default: Task)
  default_labels:               # optional (default: [argus, cost-optimization])
    - argus
    - cost-optimization
  priority_map:                 # optional — AI priority → Jira priority name
    high: High
    medium: Medium
    low: Low

Without jira.project, ticket creation fails with a clear error (the scan itself still completes).

Set the path via ARGUS_INTEGRATIONS_CONFIG if you store it elsewhere:

export ARGUS_INTEGRATIONS_CONFIG=/path/to/config/integrations.yaml

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
On first apply --confirm for a finding, Argus:

  1. Searches for an existing open ticket with label argus:<resource_id>:<policy_id>
  2. If none found — creates a new ticket with full ADF description and a snapshot fingerprint
  3. If found — compares the fingerprint and adds a comment describing what changed; the description is not rewritten

This makes apply --confirm idempotent — re-running after a re-scan either does nothing (finding unchanged) or adds one comment to the existing ticket (cost, priority, or AI reasoning changed), and never creates duplicates.

docs.title: Update on re-scan
docs.text:
If the same resource appears in a later scan with different metrics or cost:

  • Argus compares against the snapshot fingerprint embedded in the ticket description when it was created
  • It adds a comment headed Argus re-scan update — <date> listing what changed (cost, priority, AI reasoning)
  • The original description and its fingerprint are left as they were

docs.title: Close
docs.text: Argus does not auto-close tickets. When a human resolves a ticket in Jira, Argus will stop matching it on future scans (JQL filter: statusCategory != Done).

docs.title: Ticket structure (ADF)
docs.text:
Each ticket description has these sections:

Section Content Finding Resource ID, type, cloud, region, estimated monthly cost, AI priority, last activity Key Metrics Table of metrics_summary values (omitted if empty) Why Argus Flagged This AI-written waste_reason Recommendation AI-written recommendation + rightsizing hint (if applicable) Runbook Copy-paste CLI commands in a code block + "Human approval required" warning Policy policy_id, weight, source file Full Report Link to scan report (if report_url is set)

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Every apply --confirm appends a line to local_reports/audit.jsonl:

{"ts":"2026-07-05T10:23:45+00:00","proposal_id":"uuid4","resource_id":"i-0abc","resource_type":"AWS::EC2::Instance","cloud":"aws","region":"us-east-1","policy_id":"aws-ec2-stop-idle-14d","action":"stop","estimated_monthly_cost_usd":28.40,"ai_priority":"high","jira_key":"COST-42","jira_url":"https://yourorg.atlassian.net/browse/COST-42"}

The file is append-only — multiple entries for the same proposal_id represent re-scans. Use argus policies stats to aggregate it.

Override the path with ARGUS_AUDIT_LOG:

export ARGUS_AUDIT_LOG=/var/log/argus/audit.jsonl

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Every Argus ticket gets these labels automatically:

Label Purpose default_labels from integrations.yaml argus, cost-optimization unless you override them argus:<resource_id>:<policy_id> Dedup key — one open ticket per resource per policy argus-priority-<high\|medium\|low> AI-assigned priority argus-action-<action> Proposed action (stop, resize, delete, etc.)

Do not remove the dedup label

Removing argus:<resource_id>:<policy_id> from a ticket will cause Argus to create a duplicate on the next scan.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
Policies are YAML files that tell Argus which findings deserve a Jira ticket and what action to propose. Argus ships 13 bundled policies; you can add your own in config/policies/.

Installed from PyPI?

The bundled policies live in the repository's config/policies/ folder and aren't included in the pip package. Copy that folder (or config/policies.example/) into your project and set ARGUS_POLICY_DIR to it.

Starter templates

config/policies.example/ contains three annotated example policies (EC2 stop, RDS resize, GCE stop) with inline comments explaining every field and production-safe exclude defaults. Copy them to config/policies/ and edit to match your environment.

docs.title: Policy YAML format
docs.text:
version: "1"

policy_id: aws-rds-resize-high-cost-idle   # (1) unique across all files
name: Resize idle high-cost RDS instances
resource_type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance        # (2) or "*" for all types
action: resize                             # (3) must be in registry spec.actions
weight: 20                                 # (4) higher = evaluated first

conditions:                                # ALL must pass
  ai_priority: [high, medium]              # Tier 1 — AI-assigned priority
  min_estimated_monthly_cost_usd: 100      # Tier 1 — cost floor
  idle_days_min: 14                        # Tier 1 — days since last activity
  metrics:                                 # Tier 2 — metric thresholds (registry-known types)
    - metric: CPUUtilization_avg
      operator: lt
      threshold: 5.0

include:                                   # scope filter — omit to match all
  cloud_platforms: [aws]
  regions: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
  tags:
    - team: [platform, infra]

exclude:                                   # exclusion filter — omit for none
  tags:
    - environment: [prod, production]
    - argus-exempt: ["true"]
  1. policy_id must be unique across all files in the directory. Validation fails on duplicates.
  2. resource_type must match the registry exactly (e.g. AWS::RDS::DBInstance). Use * to match any type.
  3. action is validated against the registry for known resource types — an invalid action fails at load time.
  4. weight controls evaluation order. The highest-weight matching policy wins for each resource — lower-weight policies are skipped.

docs.title: Tier 1 — universal
docs.text:
Applied to all resource types. All specified conditions must pass.

Field Type Description ai_priority list AI-assigned priority: high, medium, low min_estimated_monthly_cost_usd float Resource must cost at least this per month idle_days_min int Days since last activity (requires last_activity data)

docs.title: Tier 2 — metric thresholds
docs.text:
Only applied for registry-known resource types. Each entry must specify:

Field Values Description metric string Metric key in metrics_summary (see argus policies docs <TYPE>) operator lt, gt, lte, gte, eq Comparison operator threshold float Value to compare against

All metric conditions must pass (AND logic). If a metric is not present in metrics_summary, that condition is skipped. If a metric value is not numeric, the condition fails.

Finding valid metric names

Run argus policies docs AWS::RDS::DBInstance to see all valid metrics and actions for a resource type.

docs.title: Rightsizing
docs.text:
For resize and reduce_nodes actions, Argus automatically computes a specific target recommendation from the observed CPU% in metrics_summary:

Resource type CPU% → recommendation AWS::RDS::* < 5% → db.t3.micro, < 15% → db.t3.small, < 30% → db.t3.medium AWS::EC2::Instance < 3% → t3.nano/micro, < 10% → t3.small, < 25% → t3.medium GKE / AKS clusters < 15% CPU + node count → "reduce to N nodes (target 60% utilisation)"

The recommendation appears inline in the plan table and in the Jira ticket Recommendation section. It is advisory — the human decides.

docs.title: Scope filters
docs.text:
Both include and exclude support the same fields:

Field Type Description cloud_platforms list aws, gcp, azure accounts list Account IDs / project IDs / subscription IDs (matched against the finding's account_id) regions list Region names (e.g. us-east-1, europe-west1) tags list of dicts Each entry is {key: [values]}; the resource's tag value must be one of the values

How tags entries combine differs on purpose:

  • include — the resource must match every entry (narrowing the scope).
  • exclude — matching any one entry excludes the resource. So exclude: tags: [{environment: [prod]}, {argus-exempt: ["true"]}] skips prod resources and anything tagged argus-exempt=true.

exclude takes precedence — a resource that matches both include and exclude is excluded.

Account IDs in older reports

Findings carry account_id since v0.6.0 (report schema 1.0.1). When running plan / apply against a report from an earlier version, findings have no account, so an include: accounts filter matches nothing and an exclude: accounts filter excludes nothing.

Always exclude production

All bundled policies exclude environment: [prod, production] and argus-exempt: ["true"]. Follow the same pattern in your own policies.

docs.title: Writing your own policy
docs.text:
1. Copy a bundled policy as a starting point.
  2. Set a unique policy_id.
  3. Run argus policies validate --dir config/policies — fix any errors.
  4. Run argus policies plan --report <scan.json> to see which findings it matches.
  5. Add a test in tests/core/remediation/ — see Contributing.

Safety rules

  • Never remove the argus-exempt: ["true"] exclude — it's the emergency off-switch for individual resources.
  • weight reflects your confidence in the policy, not the severity of the finding. A catch-all * policy should have a lower weight than a targeted one.
  • Prefer conservative cost floors — it's better to miss a cheap idle resource than to ticket a resource that's actually in use.

docs.title: Argus v0.7.0 Trust Release Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make Argus reports honest about what they covered and fail loudly when the environment or the model produced nothing usable, then release it as v0.7.0.

Architecture: Cloud-agnostic pieces live in core/ (selection, coverage, errors, finding confidence, prompt/window handling) and are carried by AgentLoop as attributes (loop.coverage, loop.scan_window) next to the existing loop.tracker. The AWS-only preflight lives in adapters/aws/preflight.py and runs in the Lambda/CLI entrypoint before AgentLoop.run. Report schema moves 1.0.1 to 1.1.0 by adding optional keys only.

Tech Stack: Python 3.11+, boto3, pytest, structlog, ruff + black (repo CI), mkdocs docs.

Spec: DESIGN_trust_release.md (sections 1 to 13, decisions in 12 and 13) and HANDOFF_user_feedback.md. Existing failing tests: tests/core/test_trust_regressions.py.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Strictly read-only against cloud accounts. No new write calls. No iam:List* permission for the admin-role check (name/ARN heuristic only).
  • Report schema_version becomes "1.1.0". New keys are optional; no key is renamed or removed; scan_diff must still work between a 1.0.1 and a 1.1.0 report.
  • Package version becomes 0.7.0 (core/__version__.py).
  • Exit codes: 2 budget exceeded (unchanged), 3 agent stopped without submit_findings after one re-prompt, 4 preflight failed.
  • --skip-preflight / ARGUS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=true: logs WARNING, sets preflight.skipped = true, shown in CLI summary, never default.
  • confidence is the string "low" | "medium" | "high".
  • The literal "90" must not remain as a hardcoded lookback in core/agent/prompts.py, tool schemas, or README prose about the scan window. The real value is injected from get_settings().scan.metrics_lookback_days.
  • Selection must be deterministic: same inputs, same candidate set and order (ties broken by resource_id).
  • Truncation (dropped > 0) warns by default. --strict-coverage / STRICT_COVERAGE=true makes it a failure.
  • Multi-account: one account failing preflight or the agent is recorded in scan_errors and the others continue. If every account fails, raise.
  • Repo style: line length 88, ruff and black clean, structlog for logging, no cloud SDK imports in core/.
  • No attribution lines in commit messages.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
Failure modes the spec implies that no single task's main tests would catch; each has a test in the owning task.

  1. Cap larger than discovered (no truncation): truncated is false, dropped is 0, no warning. (Task 3)
  2. Zero resources discovered: coverage is all zeros, HTML header and CLI summary render without error. (Task 3)
  3. --lookback-days 14 while the model passes days=90 in a tool call: the adapter still receives 14. (Task 4)
  4. Model submits a finding that says "zero over N days" for a resource whose metrics had has_data false: confidence is forced to "low". (Task 5)
  5. Multi-account run where account A fails preflight and account B succeeds, and where all accounts fail. (Task 6)

docs.title: Task 8: Release gate (live verification, then release)
docs.text:
Not automated; one person with a small AWS account runs this. Do not tag until every item passes.

  • [ ] Step 1: Re-run the full offline suite on the release branch: pytest -q, ruff check ., black --check .. Confirm tests/core/test_trust_regressions.py passes.
  • [ ] Step 2: Broken-setup runs against a test account, one scan each, recording the CLI output and exit code:
  • Only a LOCAL Resource Explorer index: exit 4, message names the aggregator region and fix.
  • Default view without the tags property: scan runs, report preflight shows P6_VIEW_TAGS warn, CLI prints it.
  • Index still populating: warn recorded.
  • Role without resource-explorer-2:Search: exit 4 listing the four actions.
  • Admin role: P1_IDENTITY warn recorded.
  • [ ] Step 3: Truncation run: --max-resources below the resource count with Cost Explorer resource data unavailable. Expect: coverage.selection == "stratified_by_type", every discovered type present in coverage.types, HTML header shows "Analysed X of Y", CLI prints the same.
  • [ ] Step 4: Window run: --lookback-days 14. Expect: scan_window.metrics_lookback_days == 14, no "90-day" wording in any finding, confidence at most "medium".
  • [ ] Step 5: Variance check: run the same scan 3 times with --max-resources below the resource count. Expect: identical coverage.types and candidate resource ids each time. Record the findings counts; large differences are logged as a known limitation, not hidden.
  • [ ] Step 6: Empty-result check: with a provider stub or recorded session that returns end_turn without submitting, expect exit 3 and no report claiming success.
  • [ ] Step 7: Release: merge to main, tag v0.7.0, let the existing release workflow (live-test gate before PyPI) run, verify pip install argus-cloud-optimizer==0.7.0 in a clean venv runs argus --version and a --dry-run scan.

docs.title: Argus 0.7.0 reliability plan (gap analysis + build order)
docs.text: Goal: a report a customer can rely on. Cheaper, correct, complete, repeatable. No scope limit; the release is cut when a customer re-test passes.

docs.title: Evidence (all measured on the customer's real 1000-resource run and on live accounts)
docs.text: # Gap Evidence Effect G1 Resource Explorer types (ec2:natgateway) are never mapped to registry/CloudFormation types (AWS::EC2::NatGateway) 0 of 101 real types recognised by the registry, by _is_billable, or by the CloudWatch metric table Baseline rules never fire, metric tables unused (falls back to ListMetrics), remediation policies never match, display names raw. The model silently translated names. G2 Billable filter is dead for the same reason 0 types dropped; 192 ECS task definitions, 167 security-group rules, 63 ENIs, 25 subnets, 23 IAM roles ... in the inventory Free config objects consume the analysis cap and the LLM budget G3 ReAct loop re-sends a growing conversation every turn 809 input tokens per resource, $0.0033-$0.0045 per resource 1000 resources ~ $4; coverage capped at 200 G4 Budget abort discards model work loop.py returns only rule findings on BudgetExceededError Money spent, findings lost G5 Cap picks types alphabetically when cap < number of types 101 types, cap 200 worked; cap 40 would not Arbitrary coverage G6 Cost figures are the model's guess cost_basis: estimated, no price catalog Headline dollars not reproducible G7 Waste classes with no metric signal are not checked unattached EBS volumes, unassociated Elastic IPs, stopped instances Obvious waste missed G8 Resource Explorer: 1000 results per query, tags need a view discovery_complete, P5/P6 warnings Inventory and exemption tags can be missing G9 Findings carry no evidence block HTML shows the model's prose Humans cannot verify quickly

docs.title: Build order
docs.text:
P0 correctness foundation 1. adapters/aws/type_map.py: explicit Resource Explorer -> registry type map; Resource keeps the native type; normalise at discovery. 2. Billable/config classification on real names (and cfn-style names). 3. Prove on the real customer type list: every type either recognised, classified free, or explicitly "other".

P1 evidence pipeline (the cost and completeness fix) 1. Collect evidence for every remaining resource in code (metrics, cost, activity where useful), in parallel. 2. One stateless LLM call per batch of evidence (no growing history), tool-forced submit_findings, split-and-retry on cut-off. 3. Pre-run estimate, risk-ranked order, wrap-up before the budget, never discard findings, exact "not analysed because" accounting. 4. ARGUS_ENGINE=pipeline (default) / react (legacy, used by chat).

P2 deterministic waste classes Price catalog (list prices, labelled list_price), AWS state collectors (EBS available, EIP unassociated, stopped EC2), rules for each, IAM for the new Describe calls.

P3 discovery Split a full region query by service/type to pass 1000; tag fallback through the Resource Groups Tagging API when the view has no tags.

P4 evidence in the report Per-finding evidence block (JSON + HTML), cost breakdown by cost_basis, estimate printed before spend.

P5 validation Offline eval harness from the real customer type distribution (ground-truth idle set), repeated-run determinism test, live runs on the personal account, then customer re-test.

docs.title: Definition of done
docs.text:
• A scan of the customer's real inventory shape costs well under half of today's, analyses every cost-bearing resource, and two runs agree.
  • No path discards paid-for results.
  • Every number in the headline is labelled billed / list price / model estimate.
  • Each finding shows the evidence it rests on.
